issues.spec_citation: CQL 1.5.3 Appendix B, Interval Operators: Start and End use interval boundary semantics; for open boundaries, the effective boundary is successor/predecessor of the excluded bound.
issues.evidence: SKEPTIC probe: SELECT intervalStart('{"low":1,"high":5,"lowClosed":false,"highClosed":true}') returned '1' in forced Python fallback and no-Python C++ direct extension; expected '2'. SELECT intervalEnd('{"low":"2024-01-01","high":"2024-01-31","lowClosed":true,"highClosed":false}') returned '2024-01-31'; expected '2024-01-30'. Translated CQL `start of Interval(1, 5]` and `end of Interval[@2024-01-01, @2024-01-31)` produced the same incorrect excluded boundaries.
issues.root_cause: Python fallback and native C++ intervalStart/intervalEnd returned raw low/high values for authored open bounds. Translator fallback extraction then needed to treat corrected helper outputs as closed effective bounds to avoid double-excluding half-open interval expressions.
issues.resolution: Updated Python fallback and native C++ interval helpers to return effective successor/predecessor boundaries for open bounds, rebuilt the bundled CQL DuckDB extension, and updated translator interval-bound fallback extraction to mark helper outputs closed. Added forced Python, native-loaded, translated scalar, CMS159-shaped, and no-Python C++ regression coverage.
